correctness.rationale: A biderivation is determined by f={x,y}; the relations give exactly 2xf=2yf=0, sufficient for the Jacobian bracket to descend. Its alternating Jacobiator is a triderivation, zero on triples of the two generators and hence identically zero, also in characteristic two. When char K≠2, f is in Kxy and the first-order parts of algebra automorphisms are diagonal or antidiagonal, giving precisely the sign action. In characteristic two the automorphisms have an arbitrary invertible linear part of determinant Δ and two unrestricted top-degree shears. For J=Δ(1+Hx+Ly), its inverse is Δ^−1(1+Hx+Ly). If B,C are the linear coefficients of Φ(f), then multiplying Φ(f) by that inverse adds BL+CH to the top coefficient before division by Δ; this cancels the f_1 u+f_2 v shear contribution, leaving f_3 unchanged. The three strata are distinguished by the order in the maximal ideal. The determinant-twisted linear action is transitive on nonzero linear parts (M→M/det M is an involution in dimension two). In the unit case one first normalizes the determinant and then eliminates the two linear coefficients by independent shears. This uses no roots or perfection. For the unit representative the stabilizer requires Δ=1 and both shears zero, of order q(q²−1); for the middle representative the linear part is triangular with a∈Fq×, b=0, d=1 and c unrestricted, and both shears are free, giving q³(q−1)=q²(q²−q). The socle family is fixed by every associative automorphism. Orbit-stabilizer and counting f then yield the stated totals. In the unit case with λ≠0 the derived Lie algebra spans h,x,y and is perfect; an ad(h)-stable line lies in Kh or Kx+Ky, and bracketing shows none is an ideal. Perfectness excludes a codimension-one ideal. At λ=0 the only nonzero basic bracket is [x,y]=h, giving Heisenberg. In the middle family only span{x,xy} is generated by brackets and it is abelian, while the socle family has central derived span Kxy or zero. value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification on the smallest tensor product of two nonreduced dual-number factors. Characteristic two changes not just the number of brackets but the full orbit geometry, including rank-deficient brackets inaccessible to symplectic tools. Explicit stabilizers are useful for arithmetic orbit counts, and the simple versus Heisenberg derived Lie algebra at nonzero versus zero unit parameter gives a structural distinction. This assessment does not rely on the known complex example or the standard existence of the simple Lie algebra in isolation.
